text.title: LLM-Friendly Architecture (Software Developer) — Output Contract
text.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) for the LLM-friendly architecture audit record: the repo and commit audited, the `line_limit` input (at most 300, default 250), an `audit` block with the file-size histogram and ranked oversized files each with a proposed split, directory-depth violations, barrel files, wildcard-import lint hits, the naming rubric with score and offenders, components carrying inline data, the CLAUDE.md line limit, and CI wiring; a decision that names files; evidence carrying the audit command and SHA. Validator in scripts/validate-llm-friendly-architecture.py enforces it, including the CLAUDE.md / line_limit match.

required.field: the developer accountable for the split and rename work, `role:handle`
must contain `line_limit` (integer, 100 to 300; default 250); may contain `namespace_import_allowlist` (array of module names) (r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold, r-explicit-imports-no-wildcards)

`command`, `file_size` (histogram + `oversized[]` with `path`, `lines`, `proposed_split`), `directory_depth.violations[]` (`path`, `depth` at least 4), `barrels[]`, `wildcard_imports` (`lint`, `hits[]`), `naming` (`rubric[]`, `score`, `offenders[]` with `path`, `reason`, `proposed_name`), `inline_data[]` (`path`, `lines`), `claude_md` (`present`, `line_limit`), `ci_wired` (all eight rules)
names the specific files to split, flatten, delete or rename, or commits `CLAUDE.md` and wires CI when the baseline is clean; never "reduce file sizes" (r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold)
at least two entries: the exact audit command run and the commit SHA it ran against; PR and CI-run URLs may follow (r-audit-is-reproducible-command)

forbidden.pattern: `oversized[]` entries that share a name stem with a `2` / `-part` suffix, or a `proposed_split` of "split later" — fm-01
`barrels[]` non-empty while `decision` does not name them for deletion — fm-02
any `directory_depth.violations[].depth` below 4, or a violation left out of the decision — fm-03
`naming.score` below 100 with `offenders[]` empty, or `rubric[]` empty — fm-04
`claude_md.line_limit` different from the `line_limit` input, or `claude_md.present: false` — fm-05
`evidence[]` with no audit command or no commit SHA; `audit.command` not naming an audit script — fm-06
`line_limit` above 300, or `oversized[]` containing a file at or below `line_limit` — r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold
a clean audit (no oversized, depth, barrel, wildcard, naming or inline-data findings) with `ci_wired: false` — r-audit-is-reproducible-command

list.item: `line_limit` is between 100 and 300, every `oversized[]` file is above it, sorted by size, each with a split that names target files (r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold).
`directory_depth.violations[]` lists every path deeper than 3 levels with its depth (r-directory-depth-cap).
`barrels[]` lists every `export * from` / re-export-only `index.ts`, and the decision deletes them (r-no-barrel-reexports).
`wildcard_imports.lint` names the rule run and `hits[]` lists every star or namespace import outside the allow-list (r-explicit-imports-no-wildcards).
`naming.rubric[]` is stated and `offenders[]` is non-empty whenever `score` is below 100 (r-naming-clarity-score-lists-offenders).
`inline_data[]` lists components carrying literal data blocks and the decision moves them to `src/data/` (r-static-data-extracted-from-components).
`claude_md.present` is true and `claude_md.line_limit` equals the `line_limit` input (r-claude-md-matches-audit).
`audit.command` and `evidence[]` carry the exact command and the commit SHA; `ci_wired` is true once the baseline is clean (r-audit-is-reproducible-command).
